column1: # IANA Private Enterprise Numbers — every PEN the shipped corpus depends on.
# THIS FIXTURE EXISTS BECAUSE THE PREMISE OF nl6#576 WAS THE ONE CLAIM IN IT THAT
# NOTHING COULD CHECK. Every other assertion in that change is mechanical: the
# ledger reverses against a digest, the census counts the corpus, the serve-path
# tests read values back through findResponse. "53246 is Mailteck's and 5703 is
# NVIDIA's" was prose in a commit message, and it is the fact the whole re-homing
# rests on — get it backwards and the change moves the arc from one wrong owner to
# another. nl6#541 set the precedent for this (testdata/mibs/*.tsv): extracted
# registry or tool output, checked in, with the command that produced it.
# nl6#588 WIDENED IT FROM TWO ROWS TO EVERY SHIPPED VENDOR, because the guard it
# adds — every profile may serve its OWN vendor's arc and no other — needs a
# slug-to-PEN map, and that map must be CURATED, never derived from string
# similarity between a slug and an organisation name. Six shipped pairs defeat
# name matching outright and are correct anyway (see the role column and
# ownVendorPENs' per-profile reasons): hpe_proliant_dl380 is Compaq's 232,
# dell_emc_unity is EMC Corp's 1139, nokia_7750_sr12 is 6527 ("Nokia (formerly
# 'Alcatel-Lucent')"), netapp_ontap is "Network Appliance Corporation"'s 789,
# arista_7280r3 is 30065 ("formerly 'Arastra, Inc.'"), and ibm_power_s922 is the
# bare numeric 2 — which is a PREFIX of 2011 (Huawei), 2620 (Check Point), 2636
# (Juniper) and 25461 (Palo Alto), all four of which also ship. A guard matching
# PEN strings by prefix rather than on a sub-identifier boundary reports those
# four vendors as IBM. PEN 9 (ciscoSystems) is likewise a prefix of 9999.
# The test READS this file. It does NOT fetch from iana.org: a network-dependent
# test fails closed in CI, or worse, silently skips and asserts nothing.
# Source:  https://www.iana.org/assignments/enterprise-numbers/enterprise-numbers
# Registry self-dated: (last updated 2026-08-28) — line 3 of the source file
# SHA-256 of the fetched file: e2f3c717975007e6110350014a17e359a01540c131bbf9e60b39ab2b050182fe
# The nl6#588 fetch reproduces the nl6#576 SHA-256 byte for byte and the registry
# self-date is unchanged, so the rows below and the two rows nl6#576 added come
# from the same registry snapshot.
# Regenerate, WHOLE FILE, from any machine with network access. Every row below —
# its organisation, its contact domain and its source line number — comes out of
# this and nothing is hand-typed:
#   curl -sS -o /tmp/iana-pen.txt \
#     https://www.iana.org/assignments/enterprise-numbers/enterprise-numbers
#   shasum -a 256 /tmp/iana-pen.txt   # must match the SHA-256 above
#   sed -n '3p' /tmp/iana-pen.txt     # the registry self-date
#     awk -v pen="$pen" '
#         printf "# Line %d of the source file:\n", NR
#         getline org;  sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", org)
#         getline name
#         getline mail; sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", mail)
#         sub(/^.*&/, "", mail)                 # registry writes "@" as "&"
#         printf "%s\t%s\t%s\tROLE\n", pen, org, mail
#         exit
#       }' /tmp/iana-pen.txt
#   done
# That emits every row in file order with ROLE as a placeholder; the role column
# is nl6's own annotation (see below) and is the only field a human supplies. Two
# rows need a manual note afterwards: PENs 171 and 232 carry the registry's
# literal "---none---" instead of an email, so the sub() leaves it unchanged, and
# that is correct.
# The registry format is four lines per entry: the number, the organisation, the
# contact name, then the contact email with "@" written as "&". Reproduced
# verbatim below as TSV, minus the contact NAME, which is a private individual and
# has no bearing on any assertion here.
# Columns: pen<TAB>organisation<TAB>contact_email_domain<TAB>role
# The email DOMAIN is kept because for the two rows nl6#576 turns on it is the
# corroborating evidence: an entry claiming to be NVIDIA with a contact at
# nvidia.com is a much stronger reading than the organisation string alone. IT IS
# WEAK OR ABSENT FOR SEVERAL OTHER ROWS and nothing asserts on those: two rows
# carry the registry's literal "---none---", NEC's is a 1990s bang path whose
# final domain is uunet.uu.net, and PALO ALTO NETWORKS registered a gmail.com
# address. Only TestArcPrefixesMatchTheIANARegistry checks this column, and only
# for the nvidia and mailteck rows.
# "role" is nl6's own annotation, not IANA's. It names the registry row, not a
# profile: PEN 9 covers five Cisco profiles and 5703 covers three NVIDIA ones.
# The profile-to-PEN direction lives in ownVendorPENs (snmp_own_vendor_pen_test.go)
# and is looked up here BY PEN. Five roles are not shipped vendors at all:
#   mailteck  — the arc nl6 used to serve GPU telemetry under, and must never
#               serve again (nl6#576)
#   zerna     — the arc aws_s3_storage used to answer sysObjectID with, and must
#               never serve again (nl6#588)
#   inoc      — iNOC, Inc., PEN 8714. metrics_oids.go served four SonicWALL
#               metric OIDs under it until nl6#588: a DIGIT TRANSPOSITION of
#               SonicWALL's 8741, live on the wire and enumerated into every walk
#               of that device type. The row is here so "8714 is not SonicWALL"
#               is checked-in data rather than a claim in a commit message —
#               8714 and 8741 are two lines apart in this file for exactly the
#               reason they were confusable in the first place.
#   iana-doc  — RFC 5612's documentation PEN, registered to IANA itself, which
#               aws_s3_storage and the compiled-in fallback profile now answer
#               with (nl6#588). It is allowed for THOSE TWO ONLY; it is
#               deliberately not globally permitted, or it would be a way for any
#               future profile to dodge the guard.
#   reserved  — PEN 0, "Reserved", held by IANA. 208 shipped
#               entPhysicalVendorType responses answer 1.3.6.1.4.1.0.0, which
#               resolves to no vendor at all. Not a misattribution — nobody owns
#               it — but not a vendor type either, and counted rather than
#               ignored (assertEntPhysicalVendorTypeIsNotCrossVendor).
